categories.main_business_segments: Daishin Securities operates primarily in financial investment services including retail brokerage, corporate finance, capital markets (CM), and corporate sales. Its subsidiaries extend operations into savings banking, asset management, economic research, financial investment (F&I), overseas operations in Singapore, America, and Japan, asset trust, and private equity. The company’s business segments generate revenue through securities brokerage, underwriting, asset management, real estate trust, and private equity investments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced financial technologies including proprietary trading platforms (CYBOS series, CREON), algorithmic trading, and risk management systems such as SAS Risk Dimension. It employs integrated risk management frameworks covering market, credit, liquidity, and operational risks, with specialized committees for derivatives and credit risk oversight. Daishin also leverages machine learning for its robotic customer service and employs digital innovations like AI asset management and biometric authentication.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Daishin serves a diverse customer base including individual retail investors, high-net-worth individuals, corporations, institutional investors, and overseas clients. Its markets include domestic Korean stock and derivatives markets, corporate finance clients, asset management clients, and real estate investors. Overseas operations target Asian financial hubs like Singapore and Tokyo, as well as the US market, focusing on alternative investments and private equity.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in South Korea with a network of 41 branches nationwide. It has established overseas subsidiaries in Singapore, the United States, and Japan to support international investment and asset management activities. Its geographic coverage includes key Asian financial centers and global markets, facilitating cross-border investment and alternative asset sourcing.
categories.supply_chain_position: Daishin Securities functions mainly as a midstream financial services provider, acting as an intermediary in securities brokerage, underwriting, asset management, and investment advisory. It also operates downstream in asset trust and private equity investment, managing and deploying capital into various financial and real estate assets. The company’s role encompasses capital raising, investment product distribution, and asset management services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes digital transformation and innovation in financial services, focusing on enhancing IT capabilities, developing AI-driven asset management, and expanding mobile and online trading platforms. It emphasizes risk management and regulatory compliance, investing in integrated risk systems and governance frameworks. Strategic initiatives include expanding overseas operations, diversifying revenue streams through subsidiaries, and developing differentiated financial products including private equity and real estate trusts.
categories.revenue_model: Daishin generates revenue primarily through brokerage commissions, underwriting fees, asset management fees, interest income from credit and lending operations, and gains from proprietary trading. Additional income streams include trust fees from real estate and financial trusts, private equity fund management fees, and advisory fees from corporate finance activities. The company also earns income from derivatives trading and structured financial products.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include Samsung Securities, NH Investment & Securities, Mirae Asset, and KB Securities. Daishin holds a competitive position with a market share of approximately 1.9% in stock brokerage and notable shares in futures and options markets. It is recognized for strong risk management and diversified business lines but faces intense competition from larger firms with greater capital bases and digital capabilities.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of the end of 2023, Daishin reported consolidated assets of approximately 22.6 trillion KRW, liabilities of 19.6 trillion KRW, and equity of 3.0 trillion KRW. The company achieved operating revenues of about 3.85 trillion KRW and a net income of 135.8 billion KRW, reflecting a 3.1% increase in net profit year-over-year. Despite a decline in operating income compared to the prior year, Daishin maintains strong capital adequacy with a net capital ratio of 355.1%. The company has shown steady growth and resilience amid challenging market conditions.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Daishin emphasizes its long-standing industry experience, comprehensive financial service offerings, and strong risk management capabilities as key differentiators. It leverages integrated group synergies across securities, banking, asset management, and private equity to provide tailored investment solutions. The company focuses on digital innovation, customer-centric services, and global market access to deliver stable and diversified returns. Its competitive edge also stems from specialized expertise in structured finance, real estate trusts, and alternative investments.
